What a /1 means

A /1 holds 2,147,483,648 addresses and is only seen as a large provider or registry aggregate.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /1 uses 1 network bits and leaves 31 host bits, so the block contains 2,147,483,648 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−1) − 2 = 2,147,483,648 − 2 = 2,147,483,646.

Linux

ip addr add 0.0.0.1/1 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /1?

2,147,483,646. A /1 has 2,147,483,648 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 2,147,483,646 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /1?

128.0.0.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 127.255.255.255.
